data.title: Nimnica – Holíš, a small fort of the Púchov culture above the Váh
data.excerpt: Holíš, north-east of Nimnica, is a small but find-rich hilltop settlement and small fort of the Púchov culture, around which the Váh sweeps in an arc and washes its very steep southern foot. Its position on the Trenčín–Žilina boundary was no accident: the right-bank main road along the Váh crossed this boundary here, and in the 1990s looters stripped the site completely.

children.text: North-east of Nimnica lies a small, but in terms of finds important hilltop settlement and small fort of the Púchov culture, bearing the name Holíš. According to archaeologists the crown of Holíš was fortified, and the name Hrádky is attached to its western foot in the valley of the Nimnica stream.

The Váh sweeps around the Holíš massif in an arc and washes its very steep southern foot directly. It is no wonder that the right-bank main road along the Váh avoided this bend of the Váh by crossing the Trenčín–Žilina boundary through the saddle on the southern or the northern side of the crown of Holíš. On this stretch the road was thus shortened by half. The site was introduced into the literature by A. P. Šichman. On the crown of Holíš Šichman mentions a find of pottery, which he dates to the Middle Roman period.

In the mid-1980s Holíš was also investigated by the archaeologist Jozef Moravčík together with members of an archaeological club. He reports that they identified an occupation layer with finds of pottery in the saddle between the two summits of Holíš and that there is probably a fortification on Malý Holíš as well. A sherd from the rim of a brick-red vessel was found 80 m to the west, where there is a broad plateau bounded on all sides by steep slopes.

The climb to the southern saddle of Holíš is steep, but this route is a little shorter. On the western slope of Holíš the road passes across an area occupied in the Roman period. Moravčík documented sherds of the Hallstatt period here, but above all of the Púchov culture. Šichman reports that years ago an amateur dig was supposedly carried out on the slope beside the road on the initiative of the notary, and that some metal objects were found as well. Šichman adds that this may be a brooch of the Roman period which Baron Hoening purchased from a find at Pechová. So far we have not managed to trace the illustration belonging to this.

The road from Nimnica to the more northerly saddle below Holíš has a gentler gradient than the one to the southern saddle. It passes across a settlement of the Roman period, which extends as far as the locality of Paprudie just north of the saddle and onto the eastern side of the saddle. A tradition about a golden hoard is attached to the saddle itself, and about a settlement of giants so tall that their legs reached from the saddle all the way down to the Váh. Hallstatt pottery is also attested on the slope of Paprudie. The overall extent of the occupation of Holíš is so far unknown, but it is one of the highest-lying hilltop settlements in the Váh region. The emergence of this settlement precisely on the Trenčín–Žilina boundary is no accident; it is clearly connected with the crossing of the important Váh road over this boundary.

In the 1990s Holíš became the target of raids by looters, who stripped it completely. Fortunately, at least some of the finds from that time were documented and were then published in Karol Pieta's book DIE KELTISCHE BESIEDLUNG DER SLOWAKEI (The Celtic Settlement of Slovakia). These finds, taken from the said book, can be seen in the text.
